caption: Two comparators in a ring: C1 (top middle) reads the stone I beside it and powers the stone A; C2 reads A and powers the stone T; three dust carry T's strength back into I, losing 2 per round of 4 gt. The input (a redstone block at the corner dust) holds the ring up; once it falls the ring decays 2 every 4 gt (13, 11, ... 1) and the lamp beside A stays lit until it reaches 0.

square /3 divider: study 5's dropper ring of 3 with one copper bulb, fed on both input edges by an observer (the input cell is a stone the observer powers): the bulb toggles every 3 edges, so the output is a 50% square wave at 1/3 of the input clock, for odd N too

gated pulse train: the input is a subtract comparator's rear; its output returns to its side through dust and a delay-1 repeater, so it pulses every 8 gt while the input is on (the first pulse 2 gt after it) and stops within 2 gt of the release

burst 2: a copper bulb toggles on each rising edge, its comparator changes, an observer makes that a 2 gt pulse, a delay-3 repeater stretches it to 6 gt, and a second observer pulses on both of the repeater's edges: 2 pulses 6 gt apart for any input length (min-pulse 1)

burst 3: the 2-pulse bulb burst (bulb, comparator, observer, delay-3 repeater, observer) plus an observer cascade: an observer watching the second observer toggles a second bulb, and two more observers turn that into a third pulse 6 gt after the second (found by local search from a 20-block tap design)

burst 4: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) whose pulse fans out through observers, a second bulb and a torch into delayed taps that all end in the output cell: four 2 gt pulses for any input length (found by local search from a 32-block design with three repeater taps)
